concept: Snapshot reads (atClusterTime) and history window sizing on secondaries
summary: Source-anchored research for Snapshot reads (atClusterTime) and history window sizing on secondaries. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Sizing inference: budget for the age of the chosen timestamp plus the elapsed time through the last operation, including pauses between session reads. SERVER-113128 records snapshot failures when restore tests delayed their reads and extends test retention to one hour; this is test evidence, not a production sizing recommendation. (medium confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-113128 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/long-running-queries.md

Historical implementation evidence: SERVER-47672 replaced maxTargetSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds and removed automatic history-window adjustment intended to avoid cache pressure because durable history was available. Do not apply that older adaptive-window model to the newer parameter. (low confidence)

The documented default history window is 300 seconds. A read or snapshot session that outlives retained history can fail with SnapshotTooOld; the window is a minimum retention setting, not a promise that arbitrary older timestamps remain readable. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/long-running-queries.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md

Do not generalize a recommendation to disable unused snapshot history to config servers. MongoDB explicitly warns that changing the default there can break internal operations, and setting minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds to 0 can fail internal atClusterTime snapshot reads. (low confidence)

Alibaba documents its ApsaraDB MongoDB 5.0 parameter as defaulting to 300 seconds, changeable without restart, with an exposed range of 0–600 seconds for both replica sets and shards. This is a provider/version limit, not a universal MongoDB maximum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-31)

A December 2025 practitioner account reports lower IOPS after reducing the history window from 300 to 5 seconds during a MongoDB 4.4-to-5.0 upgrade. It gives no quantified benchmark; it cannot justify that short window for long-running historical reads. (low confidence)

minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds controls the minimum retained snapshot-history window. A request whose atClusterTime is no longer in the serving server history can fail with SnapshotTooOld (239). (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/long-running-queries.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/base/error_codes.yml

Cloud.ru Managed DocumentDB exposes minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds for the shard component with an integer range of 0 to 86400 seconds. This is a provider control-plane limit, not an upstream MongoDB maximum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Sizing inference (not stated verbatim in the docs): an atClusterTime older than the oldest retained snapshot returns an error, and a session can be used for a total of 300 seconds (the default window) from its first operation to its last. So budget for the age of an explicitly selected snapshot plus elapsed session time, measured from the first operation to the last, with operational margin. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/long-running-queries.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md

MongoDB 5.0 introduced snapshot reads outside transactions on primaries and secondaries, including sharded clusters. They read majority-committed data at one point in time across shards; supported commands include find and aggregate, with distinct restricted to unsharded collections. (high confidence)

An explicit atClusterTime requests data at timestamp T. If the selected secondary has not reached T, mongod waits; maxTimeMS can bound this wait. Without explicit atClusterTime, a delayed member can return stale majority-committed data. (low confidence)

A snapshot session reuses its initial snapshot timestamp for subsequent reads. Snapshot sessions and causal consistency are mutually exclusive; do not combine atClusterTime snapshot reads with a causally consistent session. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/sessions/snapshot-sessions.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md

For self-managed mongod, minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds supports startup and runtime configuration. The documented runtime example is db.adminCommand({setParameter:1,minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds:600}). (high confidence)

Longer history retention increases disk usage, because the server must keep the history of older modified values within the window; the amount of disk used depends on the workload, so no universal retention-to-capacity ratio is given. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

MongoDB documentation directs Atlas users to Atlas Support to change minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds. Confirm that deployment-specific path before treating the self-managed setParameter example as an Atlas procedure. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Cloud.ru Managed DocumentDB exposes minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds as a shard parameter and defines it as the minimum snapshot-history retention period in seconds. This independently documents the provider-facing retention control, not upstream secondary-read correctness. (low confidence)

MongoDB 5.0 introduced snapshot reads outside transactions on primaries and secondaries, including sharded clusters. They return majority-committed data at one point in time across shards. (high confidence)

Outside multi-document transactions, read concern "snapshot" is available on primaries and secondaries for find, aggregate, and distinct (on unsharded collections); all other read commands prohibit "snapshot". Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md

A snapshot session reuses one snapshot timestamp for its related reads. Without a supplied snapshot time, the driver saves the first supported read response atClusterTime and sends it on subsequent reads. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/sessions/snapshot-sessions.md

Snapshot sessions and causal consistency are mutually exclusive. Explicit atClusterTime is prohibited inside causally consistent sessions. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md ; https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/sessions/snapshot-sessions.md

The MongoDB manual and Alibaba Cloud's ApsaraDB for MongoDB 8.0 parameter documentation both document a default minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds of 300 seconds. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/parameters-available-in-mongodb-8-0

For self-managed MongoDB, minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds can be set at startup or runtime; the manual demonstrates db.adminCommand({setParameter:1,minSnapshotHistoryWindowInSeconds:600}). The manual directs Atlas users to Atlas Support to change it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
